title: A Clinical Trial to Investigate the Safety, Efficacy, and Pharmacokinetics of Ceftobiprole Compared to Standard of Care in Children with Staphylococcus aureus Bacteremia Including Certain Heart Infections
official: A multicenter, randomized, investigator-blind, active-controlled study to evaluate the safety, tolerability, efficacy, and pharmacokinetics of ceftobiprole versus standard-of-care treatment in pediatric patients from birth to less than 18 years with Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia including right-sided infective endocarditis
summary:
Main objective: To evaluate the safety
of ceftobiprole in comparison to
SOC in pediatric patients with
SAB, including right-sided IE
conditions:
Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia (SAB), including
right-sided infective endocarditis (IE)

interventions.name: Zevtera 500 mg powder for concentrate for solution for infusion

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. 1. Pediatric age from birth to < 18 years old, with body weight ≥ 3.7 kg at the time of consent. Patients in the birth to < 2-year-old cohort should have a gestational age ≥ 37 weeks and postnatal age ≥ 3 days
2. 2. Have a parent/ LAR who can give documented informed consent and is willing and able to comply with all study procedures; assent is required of any patient who, in the Investigator’s judgment, can understand the nature of the study, or in accordance with local regulations
3. 3. SAB: a) Based on at least one blood culture obtained within 48 hours prior to randomization that is positive for S. aureus identified: (1) From subculture and overnight incubation, or (2) Directly from a blood culture positive for gram-positive cocci in clusters by any of the following*: (a) Tube coagulase, stable endonuclease, or immunological methods (b) Molecular methods (e.g., fluorescence in situ hybridization, polymerase chain reaction including the Cepheid ® GeneXpert ® system)  (c) Mass spectrometry ionization technique, namely matrix-assisted laser desorption ionization–time of flight  *Note: Non-culture detection of S. aureus from a whole blood sample from a validated technique (e.g. T2Bacteria® Panel) is acceptable for inclusion in the trial. However,  confirmatory baseline blood culture is still required prior to randomization.  OR b) Persistent SAB defined as a blood culture positive for S. aureus within 72 hours prior to randomization after ≥ 4 days (96 hours) of prior appropriate antistaphylococcal treatment Note: Evidenceof SAB (i.e., at least one blood culture positive for S. aureus) before a minimum of 4 days (96 hours) of prior appropriate anti-staphylococcal treatment is required to document the persistent SAB
4. 4. Adequate venous access for collection of protocol-specified samples and administration of study drug
5. 5. If of childbearing or reproductive potential, the patient must utilize acceptable method(s) of birth control from at least 30 days prior to Screening until at least 28 days after administration of the last dose of study drug (see Appendix 2 for patient reproductive criteria and contraception guidance)
Exclusion criteria:
1. 1.Patients with any of the following exclusion criteria are excluded from the study: 1. Receipt of systemic antibacterial treatment for S. aureus infections exceeding 48 hours within the 7 days prior to randomization.   Exceptions: Documented failure of S. aureus bloodstream clearance after ≥ 4 days (96 hours) with prior appropriate anti-staphylococcal treatment (i.e., persistent SAB)   OR Susceptibility testing results demonstrate that the patient’s S. aureus blood isolate is non-susceptible or resistant to the prior systemic antibiotic(s).
2. 10. SAB in patients with other foreign body material that cannot be removed within 7 days after randomization. Exceptions:  - Patients with non-infected central catheters and coronary stents may be included regardless of the time of implantation. - Patients with non-infected (no signs or symptoms of clinical involvement at the time of randomization) prosthetic joints, plates, spinal hardware, or other extravascular material may be included if implantation of the foreign material was performed at least 60 days before randomization. - Patients with non-infected (no signs or symptoms of clinical involvement at the time of randomization) intravascular prosthetic material or vena cava filters may be included if implantation of the foreign material was performed at least 90 days before randomization.
3. 11. Suspected or confirmed metastatic central nervous system S. aureus infection
4. 12. Immunocompromising conditions such as human immunodeficiency virus infection/acquired immunodeficiency syndrome with CD4 cell count < 750 cells/mm3 for patients < 1 year old, < 500 cells/mm3 for 1 to < 6 years old and < 200 cells/mm3 for ≥ 6 years old, bone marrow ablative therapy or bone marrow transplantation within the last 12 months, graft versus host disease in bone marrow transplantation recipients or acute rejection in solid organ transplantation recipients within the last 6 months, and severe combined immunodeficiency disorder unless successfully treated with hematopoietic stem cell transplantation and with documented immune reconstitution.
5. 13. Receipt of systemic steroids (prednisolone > 2 mg/kg per day, or equivalent) or  immunosuppressive drugs within 2 weeks prior to screening.
6. 14. Any severe, acute or chronic medical or psychiatric condition, recent neurological event, or laboratory abnormality that may increase the risk associated with study participation or administration of study treatments, or may interfere with the interpretation of study results, and which, in the judgment of the Investigator, would make the patient inappropriate for entry into this study.
7. 15. Anticipated requirement for anti-staphylococcal treatment for more than 42 days.
8. 16. Requirement or anticipated requirement between randomization and the Last follow-up  visit for potentially effective anti-staphylococcal systemic treatment that is unrelated to the SAB treatment (e.g., antibacterial prophylaxis in the context of planned surgery, treatment of acne vulgaris).
9. 17. Estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) of < 30 mL/min/1.73 m² for patients < 2 years old and < 15 mL/min/1.73 m² for patients ≥ 2 years old, or, for any age, or requirement/anticipated requirement for plasmapheresis, peritoneal dialysis, hemodialysis, venovenous dialysis, continuous renal-replacement therapy (CRRT), or other forms of renal filtration. Note: In patients <2 years old with borderline or fluctuating eGFR values between 25– 35 mL/min/1.73 m², inclusion may be permitted based on clinically stability as per Investigator’s discretion.
10. 18. History of seizures other than well-documented febrile seizures of childhood.
11. 19. Alanine transaminase (ALT) or aspartate transaminase (AST) levels > 5 × the upper limit of normal (ULN), OR total bilirubin > 2 × the ULN (except isolated unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia consistent with Gilbert’s syndrome), OR severe hepatic disease classified as Child-Pugh class C.
12. 2. Infection with S. aureus known or suspected to be non-susceptible to ceftobiprole or available SOC comparator antibiotic options.
13. 20. Patients who are pregnant or nursing.
14. 21. Patients with illicit drug use within 12 months of screening, including heroin, other opioids (unless prescribed for medical reasons unrelated to heroin substitution), cocaine /crack cocaine, and amphetamine/methamphetamine.
15. 3. Known concomitant Bloodstream or non-bloodstream infections with Gram-negative bacteria at screening.
16. 4. Left-sided IE (known or suspected to be present at the time of randomization). Note: If left-sided IE is diagnosed after commencement of study therapy, the patient must be discontinued from the study treatment and be switched to appropriate treatment per local guidelines or site-specific standard of practice.
17. 5. Contraindication to the administration of study treatments, including known clinicallyrelevant hypersensitivity to beta-lactam antibacterials.
18. 6. Participation, including patient’s mother's participation if the patient is breastfed, in any other clinical study involving investigational medication or an investigational device within the last 30 days or 5 half-lives of investigational medication, whichever is longer, prior to randomization, or any prior participation in this study.
19. 7. High probability of death within 7 days due to the underlying SAB or SAB-associated disease, or high probability of death within 28 days from an unrelated underlying disease.
20. 8. An absolute neutrophil count of <0.5 x 109/L.
21. 9. Septic shock or hypotension unresponsive to IV fluids with or without vasopressors for ≥ 4 hours
